title: How MRI Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) works, from its history and the discovery of nuclear magnetic resonance through the superconducting main magnet, gradient magnets, radio frequency pulses, hydrogen protons, and the Larmor frequency, to image reconstruction by computer. They cover the 1977 Indomitable scanner by Raymond Damadian and the rival researchers Paul Lauterbur and Peter Mansfield, Seiji Ogawa's blood-oxygen contrast work that led to fMRI, and how MRI compares with X-rays and CT. They discuss field strengths in tesla and gauss, helium cooling, the cost of machines, fMRI limits in neuroscience, MRI safety hazards with metal and projectiles, noise, gadolinium contrast dye and pregnancy concerns, and pediatric MRI. The episode ends with a listener email about reverse osmosis and electrolytic disinfection.

segments.title: Opening banter and MRI history
segments.summary: The hosts introduce MRI as the 'Wonder Machine' and recount its history, including Damadian, Lauterbur, Mansfield, and Ogawa's blood-oxygen discovery, and how MRI avoids the limits of X-rays for soft tissue.

segments.title: Magnets and field strength
segments.summary: The bore and the superconducting main magnet are described, along with tesla and gauss units, the Earth's field comparison, the cost of high-field machines, and the role of liquid helium cooling.

segments.title: Hydrogen protons, radio pulses and Larmor frequency
segments.summary: The hosts explain how the main magnet aligns hydrogen protons, how radio frequency pulses knock them out of alignment, how they relax and emit energy that differs by tissue, and the Larmor frequency. Gradient magnets select slices, and computers build the 2D or 3D image.

segments.title: fMRI and its limits
segments.summary: The hosts discuss functional MRI tracking blood flow in the brain, the criticism that it shows only rough regions rather than individual neurons, and the earlier episodes they mocked such studies, including the dead salmon study.

segments.title: MRI safety, noise, and contrast dye
segments.summary: The hosts cover MRI safety around metal and projectiles, a few rare fatal incidents, the FDA adverse event count, loud scanner noise, gadolinium contrast and its kidney clearance, pregnancy concerns, and pediatric MRI design.

segments.title: Listener mail: reverse osmosis
segments.summary: A listener named Rodney suggests an episode on reverse osmosis and electrolytic disinfection to address water-borne disease.
